common_name: Murakumo Nishiki Fatsia (Gathering Clouds Brocade Japanese Aralia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in bright partial shade to full shade; Murakumo Nishiki is a slow-growing, old Japanese heirloom selection and takes considerably longer to size up than plain green fatsia or faster variegated cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in bright shade to full shade, sheltered from strong wind and hot afternoon sun, which can bleach or scorch the gold variegation. Murakumo Nishiki is a treasured old Japanese cultivar whose deeply lobed, glossy leaves emerge golden with irregular dark green margins in spring, the gold gradually softening to chartreuse as each leaf hardens off, giving the shrub a shifting, brocade-like patchwork of color through the season. It is markedly slower and more compact than the species or common variegated selections, eventually building into a rounded multi-stemmed specimen, and rewards patience rather than the quick screening growth typical of plain fatsia. Small rounded clusters of white flowers on alien-looking spikes appear in late fall on mature plants, followed by black berries, and the shrub otherwise needs only occasional pruning to remove dead or crowded stems.

common_name: Emily Rose Aucuba (Cold-Hardy Compact Female Japanese Laurel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, organically enriched soil in partial to full shade; Emily Rose is a female selection bred for improved cold tolerance over older Aucuba japonica cultivars and needs a nearby male aucuba for the heaviest berry set.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, organically enriched soil in partial to full shade, where its glossy, dark green, toothed-margin leaves supply year-round structure in spots too dark for flowering shrubs. Emily Rose was selected for notably better cold hardiness than many older Aucuba japonica cultivars, allowing gardeners at the cooler edge of the species' range to grow it with more confidence than 'Variegata' or 'Crotonifolia'. As a female form, it develops clusters of shiny red berries that color up in mid to late winter and persist into summer when a compatible male aucuba is planted nearby for pollination. Its upright, rounded habit needs little pruning, and it tolerates dry shade, deer pressure, and heavy clay better than most broadleaf evergreens once established.

common_name: Hosoba Hoshifu Aucuba (Narrow-Leaf Star-Variegated Japanese Laurel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, in a site sheltered from winter wind and hot afternoon sun; Hosoba Hoshifu's slender leaves give it a more refined, fine-textured look than broad-leaved aucuba cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, sheltering the plant from winter wind and afternoon sun. Hosoba Hoshifu, whose Japanese name means 'narrow-leaved star-variegated,' bears slender dark green leaves only about an inch and a half wide but up to seven inches long, heavily flecked with small yellow dots, giving it a cleaner, finer texture than broad-leaved Aucuba japonica selections like 'Crotonifolia' or 'Variegata'. This narrow foliage makes it especially useful in tighter foundation plantings and Asian-inspired woodland borders where a bulkier aucuba would look too coarse. As a female selection it produces glossy, long-lasting red fruit when a male aucuba grows nearby for pollination, and it otherwise needs only occasional grooming to remove winter-damaged leaves.

common_name: Golden Girl Aucuba (Compact Gold-Speckled Hybrid Japanese Laurel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Golden Girl is a compact 1993 cross of 'Nana Rotundifolia' and 'Crotonifolia' bred for short internodes and dense, tidy growth.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where its dense, rounded habit fills small dark corners without the sprawl of larger aucuba cultivars. Golden Girl resulted from a 1993 cross between the dwarf 'Nana Rotundifolia' and the classic gold-speckled 'Crotonifolia', combining short internodes and a compact frame with richly variegated, bright yellow-speckled green leaves. As a female selection it sets clusters of large glossy red berries in fall and winter when a male aucuba is planted within pollinating distance, adding a second season of interest to its variegated foliage. Its naturally tidy size makes it well suited to shaded foundation beds, mixed containers, and small woodland gardens where a full-sized aucuba would quickly outgrow the space.

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Shishi is a rare old Japanese cultivar of unspotted, hairy-leaved leopard plant, distinct from the crimped 'Shishi Botan' and the yellow-spotted 'Aureomaculatum'.

directions: Plant divisions in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, protected from hot midday and afternoon sun that can scorch the foliage. Shishi is a rarely offered, old Japanese selection of unspotted leopard plant whose rounded leaves emerge covered in soft gray hair before aging to solid deep green, with a dramatic serrated, wavy-edged margin that sets it apart from smooth-leaved farfugium and the crimped, parsley-like 'Shishi Botan'. In fall it sends up stalks roughly two feet tall topped with bright yellow daisy-like flowers, adding late-season color above the low foliage mound. It forms slow-spreading clumps over time and is best used as a textural shade-garden accent or in a large container where its subtle, unspotted foliage can stand on its own.
